title: High Court refuses interim protection to Abhishek Banerjee's aide Sumit Roy; MP to face police questioning
dek: Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya said protection would serve no purpose while Roy is in custody. Abhishek Banerjee is due at Girish Park police station on Friday in a separate case.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Calcutta High Court on Thursday refused interim protection to Sumit Roy, the personal assistant of Trinamool Congress national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, who had asked the court to stop the state from registering fresh criminal cases against him or taking coercive steps in the cases already filed. Mr Banerjee is himself due to appear for questioning at Kolkata's Girish Park police station at noon on Friday in a separate case.

Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya said the concerns raised in Mr Roy's petition "need not be examined at this stage" and that a writ court's powers in criminal matters must be used sparingly where other remedies are available, according to reports of the hearing. Because Mr Roy is already in custody, protection in the other cases "will not serve the purpose", the judge said, according to reports.

## What the petition said

Mr Roy, represented by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, told the court he faced five FIRs registered in July and August at the Diamond Harbour and Jibantala police stations, four of them on complaints by a BJP leader and his associates, according to reports. He is in custody in one and sought protection in the other four, so that he could pursue his remedies in the case in which he is held. He argued that he was being persecuted for political reasons after the BJP came to power in the state in May, that some complaints concerned events up to ten years old, and that they amounted to "fishing and roving" inquiries without specific acts alleged against him.

The allegations in the cases include running unlicensed medical camps, helping to supply fake educational certificates, a 2018 political assault and a 2020 attack linked to cyclone relief money, according to reports. Additional Advocate General Rajdeep Mazumder appeared for the state.

## Background

Mr Roy was arrested by the state's Criminal Investigation Department in September in a land case, after the Supreme Court refused him anticipatory bail, and has since been shown arrested in other cases, including one over alleged soil theft in South 24 Parganas, according to reports. Questioning of Mr Roy led police to a Trinamool office in Sarisha, South 24 Parganas, where they said they recovered more than Rs 1 crore in cash this month, according to reports. The Trinamool Congress says the cases are fabricated and has alleged that Mr Roy was threatened during questioning, according to reports.

Mr Banerjee, the MP for Diamond Harbour, has been summoned in a case registered at Girish Park police station on 31 October on a woman's complaint that his public remarks threatened a serving IPS officer and other police personnel, according to reports. He has said Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's government is using the police to target opposition leaders. He appeared at Bhawanipore police station on 14 November in another case, over a social media post, and said afterwards he had "nothing to hide", according to reports.

## What happens next

Mr Roy can pursue bail and other remedies before the trial courts in each case. Mr Banerjee's appearance at Girish Park on Friday will be the second time this month he has been questioned by Kolkata Police. The High Court has also issued him a show-cause notice in criminal contempt proceedings over remarks about the judiciary, and has reserved its order on his challenge to the reduction of his security cover, according to reports.
